title: Affinity Purification of Label-free Tubulins from Xenopus Egg Extracts
protocol: Prepare egg extracts from different frog species in a temperature-controlled lab-space maintained between 18°C–20°C.
Coat all glass and plastic-ware by swirling a 0.2% gelatin % (w/v) solution for X.t. extract preparation.
Discard gelatin solution from beakers after use.
Collect laid eggs in a 0.8 or 1 L glass beaker and keep batches separate if possible.
Pour off any residual buffer/water from the eggs and wash several times in 1× MMR (0.5× MMR for X.b.).
Remove lysed and puffy eggs using a Pasteur pipette.
Discard batches of eggs with more than 10% lysed or activated.
Add Dejelly Buffer to the eggs and gently swirl to ensure uniform dejellying.
Exchange the solution after 2.5 min and wash again with fresh Dejelly Buffer.
Upon successful dejellying, pour off as much Dejelly Buffer as possible while ensuring that the eggs are not exposed to air.
Add CSF-XB to the beaker and gently swirl the eggs.
Decant the CSF-XB and wash 2–3 times with CSF-XB Buffer.
Exchange the CSF-XB for CSF-XB+ buffer containing protease inhibitor and gently swirl.
Preload an ultracentrifuge tube with 1 ml of CSF-XB+ buffer and Cytochalasin D as specified (X.l. and X.b.: 10 μL of 10 mg/mL; X.t.: 5 μL of 10 mg/mL).
Carefully load eggs into the ultracentrifuge tube using a cut plastic Pasteur pipette without exposing them to air.
Fill the tube all the way to the top if possible, especially when mixing eggs from different batches.
Transfer the ultracentrifuge tube into a polypropylene tube using forceps.
Add a few drops of buffer into the polypropylene adaptor before transferring the tube containing eggs.
Set the clinical centrifuge to 18°C for X.l. and X.b. eggs or to 16°C for X.t. eggs.
Spin X.l. and X.b. eggs at 500 rpm for 30 s, followed by 2,000 rpm for 90 s.
Spin X.t. eggs at 200 rpm for 30 s, followed by 800 rpm for 90 s.
Remove any residual buffer on top of the tightly packed eggs after the spin.
Transfer the tubes into rubber adaptors.
Set the clinical centrifuge to 11,000 rpm in a JS-13.1 swinging bucket rotor (19,000 × g).
Spin the samples for 20 min at the set conditions.
Centrifugation should start at room temperature or 18°C.
Cool the centrifuge during the spin to reach 4°C for X.l. egg extracts.
Maintain a constant temperature of 16°C–18°C for X.b. and X.t. egg extracts.
Set the acceleration settings on the centrifuge to maximum.
Set the deceleration step to slow and turn off the brake.
Remove the thin-wall tube with fractionated eggs from the polypropylene adaptor after spinning.
Maintain all equipment at appropriate temperature; keep syringes, needles, forceps, tubes, etc., on ice for X.l. and X.b. extracts.
Keep equipment between 16°C–20°C for X.t. extracts.
Puncture the tube near the bottom of the cytoplasmic layer with a syringe and 18G-needle.
Rotate the needle so that the opening faces up.
Aspirate the cytoplasmic fraction gently using the syringe.
Remove the needle and gently expel the extract into an Eppendorf tube.
Keep extracts on ice throughout purification, except X.t. egg extract at 16°C for assembly purposes.
Add Cytochalasin D (1:1,000) and protease inhibitors (1:100) to the X.l. extract.
Add Cytochalasin D (1:500) and protease inhibitors (1:200) to the X.b. and X.t. extracts.
Gently mix the extracts with a cut pipette tip.
Take a western blot sample of the extract for quality control (optional).
Proceed immediately to the tubulin purification step.
Dilute egg extract 1:1 with 1× BRB80 to achieve a final volume of 8 mL.
Take a 10 μL sample "lysate" for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Add 3 μL benzonase (25 U/μL) to the egg extract.
Add DTT to the egg extract to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM.
Mix the egg extract carefully by slowly pipetting up and down with a cut pipette tip.
Split the diluted egg extract into two ice-cold polycarbonate ultracentrifuge tubes.
Adjust the weight of the split extracts to be equal by adding small drops of 1× BRB80.
Centrifuge the adjusted extracts at 80,000 rpm (440,000 × g) in a pre-cooled MLA-80 rotor at 2°C for 30 minutes.
Take a 10 μL sample of the post-centrifugation extract for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Wash tubing with 20% ethanol.
Wash tubing with ultra-pure water.
Wash tubing with wash buffer.
Connect the TOG column to the peristaltic pump and tubing.
Equilibrate the TOG column with 10 CV of 1× BRB80 at a flow rate of 1 CV/min.
Cycle the cleared lysate through the TOG column at a flow rate of 0.5 CV/min for 20 minutes.
Take a 10 μL sample of “flow-through” for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Wash with 2 CV wash buffer to clear out most of the extract from the TOG column.
Take a 100 μL sample of “wash 1” for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Change the flow rate to 1 CV/min.
Wash with 10 CV wash buffer.
Take a 100 μL sample of “wash 2” for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Wash with 3 CV ATP wash buffer.
Take a 100 μL sample of “ATP wash” for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Incubate for 15 min.
Start equilibrating the PD-10 desalting columns 3× with ice-cold desalting buffer.
Wash with 3 CV ATP wash buffer.
Take a 100 μL sample of “wash 4” for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Wash with 10 CV wash buffer.
Take a 100 μL sample of “wash 5” for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Check this wash for the presence of proteins either by Bradford assay or A280.
If you detect protein, additionally wash with 4 CV wash buffer.
Take a 100 μL sample of “wash 6” for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Decrease flow rate to 0.25 CV/min.
Elute tubulin with 3 CV elution buffer into 15× 1 mL fractions.
Check each fraction for protein using a Bradford assay or A280 measurement.
Pool the fractions with the highest protein concentration.
Desalt pooled fractions via PD-10 columns using ice-cold desalting buffer.
Take a 10 μL sample of pooled peak elutions for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Equilibrate one 4 mL Amicon Ultra-4 concentration column with desalting buffer by spinning it twice for 3 min at 4,000 rpm (3,220 × g) in a clinical centrifuge at 2°C.
Concentrate the tubulin to at least 20 μM using the equilibrated Amicon Ultra-4 concentration column by spinning in a clinical centrifuge at 4,000 rpm (3,220 × g) at 2°C.
Take a 2 μL sample of desalted and concentrated solution for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Measure the final protein concentration of concentrated tubulin.
Flash-freeze tubulin samples in liquid nitrogen.
Store aliquoted tubulin samples at -80°C.
Clean the TOG column by washing with 5 CV 1× PBS at 1 CV/min.
Reduce flow rate to 0.5 CV/min and wash with 10 CV 10× PBS.
Wash the TOG column with 10 CV column storage buffer.
Cap the TOG column tightly without introducing air bubbles.
Store the capped TOG column in a 50 mL Falcon tube at -20°C.
Proceed with SDS-PAGE for quality control.
Conduct western blot analysis for quality control.
